I joined the surgery around summer last year. Ive had issues with my health for the past 4+ years and have understood that the NHS is under strain and has long waiting times etc.

Unfortunately, over the past 8/9 months, my health issues have got substantially worse and I then joined the surgery. From the start I struggled with the online booking system but thats okay. It seems when you need an emergency appointment, it is almost impossible to get one. I recently rang up to try and get an appointment and was told that I would get a call back. When I did get the call back I was told that it is not urgent (even though I have been badgering the surgery for the past 8/9 months) and I have to wait for a future appointment, which is a month wait for a phone call appointment! They send links for appointments that have nothing available etc. I have been missing work/lost my social life/cancelled holidays/dont feel safe to drive all due to the way I have been feeling, so to be told that its not urgent is really great. I have also contacted privately to try and get through to somebody but this has come to nothing.

I would be okay with this if it was worth the wait. On the handful of occasions I have managed to get in, there have been a few times when I have left feeling like Im not listened to, fobbed off, spoken to very patronisingly or told to make a diary. This has been nurses and receptionist as well.

Ive only managed to get 1 set of blood tests in all this time! No other tests have been done. No referrals sent off (even though it was promised). I will give credit to one doctor - Kathryn Hayman. She is the only one who has ordered tests and actually listened etc but the wait to get back in to see her is too long!

I thought I might be the only one who feels like this but after seeing other reviews I'm clearly not! I understand that all GPs/nurses are all under pressure, but if things were done properly early on then there wouldnt be people coming back so
